## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Godharājajātaka* (Ja 325), translated as *The Lizard King*, is a birth story in the Pali Jātaka collection. Set at Jetavana, the Buddha recounts the tale regarding a deceptive monk described as a cheating rogue [Fausböll 1883]. In the story of the past, the Bodhisatta was born as the king of the lizards (*godharājā*), who confronts and exposes a hypocritical ascetic (*kūṭajaṭila*) [Fausböll 1883]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha connects the past lives with the present: the deceitful ascetic is revealed to be the cheating monk (*kuhakabhikkhu*), and the lizard king was the Buddha himself [Fausböll 1883].

 At the verse and passage level, it corresponds to verse 394 of the Pali *Dhammapada* (dhp394) and another Pali story, the *Godhajātaka* (Ja 138), as well as cross-tradition parallels in the Sanskrit *Udānavarga* (UV 33, *Brāhmaṇavarga*), the Tibetan *Udānavarga* (Uv Kg 33), Gāndhārī Dharmapada recensions (G-Dhp 1–50 and G3-Dhp 61–70), and Chinese translations including T 210.35, T 212.34, and T 213.33. In internal Pali textual reuse, DharmaNexus identifies significant shared segments between this narrative and both the *Dhammapada-aṭṭhakathā* (8 matches) and the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (6 matches) [DharmaNexus].
